guideline: Sentence-level AIS (Attributable to Identified Sources) framework
Sentence-level AIS (Attributable to Identified Sources) framework
Annotators evaluate coherence on a 5-point Likert scale and (for LFQA) helpfulness; then judge attribution via the Attributable to Identified Sources (AIS) framework.
Annotators rate text coherence, helpfulness (for LFQA), and citation support (full/partial/no support) using provided criteria.

Annotators are asked to evaluate text coherence on a 5-point Likert scale, and in the LFQA setting also its helpfulness in addressing the query. Next, annotators proceed to evaluate the quality of citations. We follow the sentence-level attribution evaluation protocol from , which extends the Attributable to Identified Sources (AIS;  human evaluation framework of attribution to the sentence-level. Annotators judge whether each output sentence is fully supported by its attribution, scoring 1 for full support and 0 otherwise.

overall_notes: Paper presents a novel 'Attribute First, then Generate' approach for fine-grained attribution in grounded text generation. The extraction was generally accurate but contained some redundancy and needed normalization. Key contributions include local attribution methodology evaluated on both MDS and LFQA tasks using automatic metrics and comprehensive human evaluation.
